processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Ingots with nominal composition Fe-35Mn-xAl-5Cu (at.%, x = 19) produced by melting high-purity (>99.9 %) raw materials in a vacuum induction furnace under an argon atmosphere.

processing_steps.reduction_ratio: plates with a thickness of 4 mm
processing_steps.processing_steps_notes: Homogenized ingots hot-rolled into plates with a thickness of 4 mm.
Plates were cut into 10 × 5 × 2 mm³ samples using electrical discharge machining for Vickers hardness measurements and microstructure characterizations.
Solution treated at 1100 °C for 10 min under an argon atmosphere, followed by oil quenching.
Solution-treated 19Al aged at 625 °C for 6 h, followed by water quenching.

structures.overall_structure: For the 19Al alloy, at aging temperatures of 600 °C and above the α matrix had almost completely transformed into β-Mn after just 1 h of aging; numerous fine precipitates (BCC and FCC phases) were distributed within the β-Mn once the α matrix had fully transformed. Therefore the 19Al sample aged at 625 °C for 6 h consists of a β-Mn matrix with fine BCC and FCC Cu-rich precipitates.

phases_present.morphology: fine precipitates/precipitates distributed within the β-Mn
fine precipitates at the β-Mn interfaces

interfaces.phase_evolution: α → α + FCC Cu-rich phase → α-Mn + β-Mn + BCC phase → β-Mn + BCC phase + FCC Cu-rich phase
interfaces.interface_notes: The BCC phase forms at β-Mn interfaces due to the enrichment of the BCC-stabilizing element Al around the β-Mn interfaces, while the FCC Cu-rich phase forms because of the limited solubility of Cu in Fe-based alloys and the expulsion of Cu from β-Mn during precipitation and growth. Both precipitates have intrinsic hardness lower than β-Mn.

measurement_conditions.other_conditions: Vickers hardness measured on an HVS-1000 digital microhardness tester with a load of 9.8 N for 15 s; each sample tested 5 times and the value is the average of 5 measurements.

characterization_methods.measurement_conditions: Load 9.8 N, dwell 15 s; each sample repeatedly tested 5 times and the hardness given as the average of 5 measurements
characterization_methods.purpose: Measure Vickers hardness of 19Al after aging at 625 °C for 6 h
characterization_methods.key_findings: 870.7 ± 16.1 HV for the 19Al alloy aged at 625 °C for 6 h; all aged values are far above the solution-treated baseline of 263.8 ± 1.1 HV.

characterization_methods.instrument_or_setup: ZEISS Sigma 300 SEM operated at 5 kV
characterization_methods.purpose: Identify precipitation of second phases (α-Mn, β-Mn) in aged samples
characterization_methods.key_findings: In the 19Al alloy from 600 °C and above (relevant to 625 °C aging) the α matrix had almost completely transformed into β-Mn after just 1 h, and numerous fine precipitates were observed within the β-Mn after full transformation.

unmapped_findings: For the 19Al alloy the optimal aging temperature range to achieve ultra-high hardness is reported as 575 °C–625 °C (b0038), so 625 °C/6 h falls within the optimal ultra-high-hardness window for this alloy.
Fig. 2 (figure_002) contour map for the 19Al alloy describes the 625 °C series as plateauing near 800–860 HV, consistent with the Table 4 value of 870.7 ± 16.1 HV at 625 °C/6 h.

The elastic modulus E of the 19Al alloy, measured through compressive stress-strain curves, is 181 GPa (b0023); this value was used in Eq. (1) for the indentation fracture-toughness calculation of the hardest (917.8 HV) 19Al sample.

The hardest 19Al sample (peak 917.8 HV, achieved at 600 °C for 10 h — not the 625 °C/6 h condition) had a K_IC of 3.5 MPa·m^1/2 with an average indentation crack length of 35 μm (b0061), and a β-Mn intrinsic nanoindentation hardness of 12.5 ± 0.4 GPa with 17.5 at.% Al dissolved in β-Mn (b0060, figure_014). These values belong to the peak-hardness condition of the 19Al alloy, not to the 625 °C/6 h sample.

For the 19Al alloy aged at 650 °C for 6 h (a different condition from this sample), the combined volume fraction of FCC Cu-rich and BCC precipitates was 6.5 % and the Vickers hardness was 810.9 HV (b0069).
